name: Transient Ischemic Attack
definition: Transient focal neurological dysfunction caused by ischemia without acute infarction, carrying significant early stroke risk.

typical: Symptoms resolve but remain clinically important

redFlags.item: Ongoing deficit should be treated as possible stroke
Atrial fibrillation or major vascular symptoms

investigations.MRI: MRI with diffusion imaging may identify infarction; vascular imaging guides management.

amber: Do not reassure solely because symptoms resolved.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Transient Pakshaghata-like symptoms should never delay modern TIA/stroke pathway.

patientEducation.summary: Transient focal neurological dysfunction caused by ischemia without acute infarction, carrying significant early stroke risk.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
